title: POC Weekly Sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on access and environment readiness. Customer confirmed VPC peering request and SSO details; SRE working through infra permissions. SE (Priya) walked through priming tests, batching and KV cache recommendations; noted a few infra blockers for load tests. Action items include sending SOC2 + network diagram, enabling service account for load tests, scheduling a 100k-token throughput run next week; pricing/commits to be discussed after baseline benchmarks.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 and security pack (Alex) by 2026-11-13
SRE (Sofia) to confirm VPC peering CIDR and open ports by 2026-11-12
Schedule 100k-token throughput run with Redwood SE week of 2026-11-16
Alex to share preliminary cost model for dedicated vs hosted by 2026-11-15
action_items: Alex Kim: send SOC2 + network diagram; due 2026-11-13
Sofia Martinez: confirm VPC peering CIDR and open ports; due 2026-11-12
Priya Raman: prepare load-test config and runbook; due 2026-11-15
Jordan Lee: provide sample prompt set and success criteria; due 2026-11-14
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-11-11
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marcus Bell (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (NexaHead ML), Sofia Martinez (Nexa SRE), Ethan Park (Nexa CTO)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick checks — can you hear me?
[00:04] Jordan Lee: yep, loud and clear. thanks.
[00:08] Alex Kim: great. Agenda today — onboarding progress, access setup, and environment readiness for the POC. also we'll review the early priming results and outline next steps.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: before we start, SSO details — we tried the SAML metadata upload but got a certificate error, so we'll share updated certs after this call.
[00:27] Priya Raman: ok that matches what we saw. for SSO the IdP metadata needs to include the cert chain; if you paste it in the console it validates.
[00:36] Ethan Park: on the VPC peering, our networking team wants the exact CIDRs and port list. we do not want wide open access.
[00:44] Marcus Bell: understood — we'll share a minimal port list: 443 outbound, and a small set of ephemeral ports for health checks. we'll put that in the network diagram.
[00:52] Jordan Lee: good. on the POC work, we ran the sample inference locally with the redwood dedictaed config from the doc and saw roughly 120ms p50 for 256 tokens on g5-like hardware, but the throughput dropped under batch loads.
[01:05] Priya Raman: a couple notes — first, the p50 number sounds right but did you mean p95? p50 will be optimistic. second, when you say throughput drops, is that due to small batch sizes or KV cash miss? (laughs)
[01:18] Jordan Lee: ha, yes kv cash — I mean KV cache misses. we didn't configure prefix caching so most requests missed; once we enabled prefix caching in the poc harness throughput improved.
[01:30] Priya Raman: exactly — our recommendation is to enable prefix/KV caching for production-like prompts. also tune batch size; for your median prompt length we recommend batch=8-16 and a max concurrent requests setting.
[01:44] Sofia Martinez: there's a permissions blocker — our CI runner doesn't have the service account to run load tests against the private env. we can create one but need a template for least privilege.
[01:54] Alex Kim: we'll send a service account template and an IAM role example. Marcus will add the least-privilege policy to the repo.
[02:03] Marcus Bell: yep, I'll drop that in the shared drive after the call.
[02:08] Jordan Lee: about security: can you reconfirm how logs are handled in the private deployment? we need audit logs to be delivered to our splunk/kms.
[02:16] Priya Raman: for Redwood Private we can ship audit logs to your S3 bucket or push to your SIEM via syslog — and encryption at rest uses your KMS key if you provide it. for hosted we have a different pipeline but we can enable log-forwarding.
[02:29] Ethan Park: we need SOC 2 type II docs and the network diagram before we do the full ramp.
[02:35] Alex Kim: noted —Alex to send SOC2, compliance pack, and network diagram.
[02:39] Jordan Lee: thanks. also curious about failover — if the main region hits capacity, can we route to a cheaper model or another region automatically?
[02:48] Priya Raman: yes — smart routing supports region fallback and model variant fallback. you can set a policy: latency-first or cost-first. if capacity constrained we can route to a quantized variant with slightly lower quality.
[02:59] Sofia Martinez: does that affect context window size? we rely on 4k tokens for the EHR prompts.
[03:05] Priya Raman: good call — quantized variants often preserve the same context window but there are edge cases; we'll validate with your 4k prompt set during the benchmark.
[03:14] Jordan Lee: on benchmarking, we ran a quick run at 10k tokens and saw costs bleeding; want to see the dedicated numbers vs hosted with batching.
[03:23] Alex Kim: we'll prepare a cost model comparing reserved dedicated vs hosted burst pricing with your throughput numbers. may also recommend quantization for non-sensitive pipelines.
[03:33] Ethan Park: any regulatory constraints on quantization? we can't lose PHI protections.
[03:38] Priya Raman: quantization is model-layer only — it doesn't change where data sits. for Private deployments you control the keys and storage. for hosted we'll sign an NDA for PHI and can discuss redaction options.
[03:49] Jordan Lee: ok. can we talk about the load test schedule? we want a 100k-token throughput run to simulate peak daytime load.
[03:56] Priya Raman: we recommend doing a step test: 10k, 25k, 50k, then 100k. need the service account and VPC peering to be ready.
[04:05] Sofia Martinez: re ports — we'll open 443 outbound, allow the health-check ports you share, and set up VPC peering. will confirm CIDR by Thursday.
[04:14] Alex Kim: perfect. for the runbook — Priya will own test config; Marcus will own infra setup. Jordan will own the prompt set and pass/fail criteria.
[04:22] Jordan Lee: I'll put the prompt set in the shared folder and flag which prompts require 4k context.
[04:28] Ethan Park: about metrics — we want per-route latency, token counts, and per-request cost breakdowns. your console can show that right?
[04:36] Marcus Bell: yep — Console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost and latency breakdowns. we'll send a screenshot. sometimes the export CSV columns get misnamed but we will annotate.
[04:46] Jordan Lee: small nit — the sample SDK in the docs had a typo on the retry backoff parameter, caused a flapping test.
[04:52] Priya Raman: thanks, we'll patch that doc. good catch.
[04:56] Sofia Martinez: timeline wise, if we finish infra by next Thu can we do the 100k run the following week?
[05:03] Alex Kim: yes that works; tentative run week of 2026-11-16.
[05:07] Jordan Lee: are there any known regressions with the model variant you're recommending? we've seen a hallucination spike previously.
[05:13] Priya Raman: we monitor QA regression tied to prompt sets; we'll run evals pre/post rollout. we'll also enable quality alerts if you want automatic rollback on metric drift.
[05:23] Ethan Park: great. last thing — pricing: can you share a sample committed pricing for dedicated capacity?
[05:29] Alex Kim: I can share a starter pricing model — small reserved pool pricing and burst rates; Alex to send after call.
[05:35] Jordan Lee: thanks. that covers it.
[05:38] Alex Kim: recap — action items and next steps. send SOC2 pack, network diagram, service account template, schedule load tests. anything else?
[05:46] Jordan Lee: no, that's it. thanks everyone.
[05:48] Alex Kim: thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and the cost model. bye.
[05:52] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional transcription errors ("dedictaed" for dedicated, "KV cash" for KV cache); speaker labels approximate.
